text: This tortoise is a hundred ninety-four. But part of him still acts young.
How? Scientists just read his DNA.
His name is Jonathan. He hatched before the first photo of a person was ever taken.
His kind usually lives about a hundred years. He nearly doubled it.
So scientists swabbed his cheek. First try? Mouth bacteria.
But try two worked. Two hundred eighty-seven rare gene changes tied to aging.
In genes that fix broken DNA and protect chromosome tips.
And the switches on his cell batteries? Still neat, like a young tortoise.
Now, it's one tortoise. Nobody knows yet if these genes caused his long life.
So next, scientists want his blood. Because his secret might show how all of us age.
Not bad for a guy older than the camera.
